content:
We need to extract formal theory: list of rules with modality, target, condition, exception, temporal, participants, quote. Must be JSON only, no markdown. Must follow policy. Let's parse policy for rules.

Policy sections:

- As a retail agent, you can help users: list of allowed actions. That's a PERMIT? Actually it's describing capabilities. Could be PERMIT to help users with those actions.

- At the beginning of the conversation, you have to authenticate the user identity by locating their user id via email, or via name + zip code. This has to be done even when the user already provides the user id. => REQUIRE to authenticate before any action.

- Once the user has been authenticated, you can provide the user with information about order, product, profile information, e.g. help the user look up order id. => PERMIT to provide info after authentication.

- You can only help one user per conversation (but you can handle multiple requests from the same user), and must deny any requests for tasks related to any other user. => REQUIRE to only help one user; FORBID to help other users.

- Before taking any action that updates the database (cancel, modify, return, exchange), you must list the action details and obtain explicit user confirmation (yes) to proceed. => REQUIRE: before DB update actions, list details and get explicit confirmation.

- You should not make up any information or knowledge or procedures not provided by the user or the tools, or give subjective recommendations or comments. => FORBID to make up info or give subjective recommendations.

- You should at most make one tool call at a time, and if you take a tool call, you should not respond to the user at the same time. If you respond to the user, you should not make a tool call at the same time. => REQUIRE: at most one tool call at a time; cannot mix tool call and response.

- You should deny user requests that are against this policy. => FORBID to comply with requests against policy? Actually "deny user requests that are against this policy" means you must deny such requests. So FORBID to fulfill requests against policy.

- You should transfer the user to a human agent if and only if the request cannot be handled within the scope of your actions. To transfer, first make a tool call to transfer_to_human_agents, and then send the message 'YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.' to the user. => PERMIT to transfer when request out of scope; REQUIRE to follow that procedure.

Domain basic: times EST etc not a rule.

User profile: not rule.

Product: not rule.

Order: not rule.

Generic action rules:

- Generally, you can only take action on pending or delivered orders. => FORBID to take action on other statuses (processed, cancelled). So FORBID action on orders not pending/delivered.

- Exchange or modify order tools can only be called once per order. Be sure that all items to be changed are collected into a list before making the tool call!!! => REQUIRE: exchange/modify tools only once per order; condition: collect all items before call.

Cancel pending order:

- An order can only be cancelled if its status is 'pending', and you should check its status before taking the action. => REQUIRE: check status pending before cancel; FORBID cancel if not pending.

- The user needs to confirm the order id and the reason (either 'no longer needed' or 'ordered by mistake') for cancellation. Other reasons are not acceptable. => REQUIRE: user must confirm order id and reason; reason limited to those two; FORBID other reasons.

- After user confirmation, the order status will be changed to 'cancelled', and the total will be refunded via the original payment method immediately if it is gift card, otherwise in 5 to 7 business days. (This is outcome, not rule.)

Modify pending order:

- An order can only be modified if its status is 'pending', and you should check its status before taking the action. => REQUIRE: check status pending before modify; FORBID modify if not pending.

- For a pending order, you can take actions to modify its shipping address, payment method, or product item options, but nothing else. => PERMIT to modify those three; FORBID other modifications.

### Modify payment

- The user can only choose a single payment method different from the original payment method. => REQUIRE: only single different payment method.

- If the user wants the modify the payment method to gift card, it must have enough balance to cover the total amount. => REQUIRE: gift card balance sufficient.

- After user confirmation, the order status will be kept as 'pending'. The original payment method will be refunded immediately if it is a gift card, otherwise it will be refunded within 5 to 7 business days. (outcome)

### Modify items

- This action can only be called once, and will change the order status to 'pending (items modifed)'. The agent will not be able to modify or cancel the order anymore. So you must confirm all the details are correct and be cautious before taking this action. In particular, remember to remind the customer to confirm they have provided all the items they want to modify. => REQUIRE: modify items only once; after that cannot modify/cancel; must confirm all details; remind customer to confirm all items.

- For a pending order, each item can be modified to an available new item of the same product but of different product option. There cannot be any change of product types, e.g. modify shirt to shoe. => PERMIT to modify item to same product different option; FORBID change product type.

- The user must provide a payment method to pay or receive refund of the price difference. If the user provides a gift card, it must have enough balance to cover the price difference. => REQUIRE: provide payment method for price diff; gift card sufficient balance.

Return delivered order:

- An order can only be returned if its status is 'delivered', and you should check its status before taking the action. => REQUIRE: check status delivered before return; FORBID return if not delivered.

- The user needs to confirm the order id and the list of items to be returned. => REQUIRE: user confirm order id and list items.

- The user needs to provide a payment method to receive the refund. => REQUIRE: provide payment method for refund.

- The refund must either go to the original payment method, or an existing gift card. => REQUIRE: refund to original payment method or existing gift card; FORBID other.

- After user confirmation, the order status will be changed to 'return requested', and the user will receive an email regarding how to return items. (outcome)

Exchange delivered order:

- An order can only be exchanged if its status is 'delivered', and you should check its status before taking the action. In particular, remember to remind the customer to confirm they have provided all items to be exchanged. => REQUIRE: check status delivered; remind customer to confirm all items.

- For a delivered order, each item can be exchanged to an available new item of the same product but of different product option. There cannot be any change of product types, e.g. modify shirt to shoe. => PERMIT exchange to same product different option; FORBID change product type.

- The user must provide a payment method to pay or receive refund of the price difference. If the user provides a gift card, it must have enough balance to cover the price difference. => REQUIRE: provide payment method for price diff; gift card sufficient.

- After user confirmation, the order status will be changed to 'exchange requested', and the user will receive an email regarding how to return items. There is no need to place a new order. (outcome)

Also generic: you should not make up any information... etc.

We need to produce JSON with rules array. Each rule includes modality, target (action), condition, exception, temporal (anchor and order), participants, quote.

We need to extract exact verbatim quote from policy that proves each rule.

We must not invent elements. Use null when absent.

We need to decide which rules to include. Likely include each distinct rule from policy. Could be many. But we must output only JSON. Let's try to capture key rules.

We'll produce maybe ~15 rules.

We need to include quote exactly as in policy. Must copy text exactly.

Let's list rules with quotes.

1. Authenticate user at beginning: "At the beginning of the conversation, you have to authenticate the user identity by locating their user id via email, or via name + zip code. This has to be done even when the user already provides the user id."

Modality: REQUIRE. Target: authenticate user. Condition: at beginning of conversation. Exception: null. Temporal: anchor: "beginning of the conversation", order: "BEFORE" any other action? Could be BEFORE any help. We'll set temporal anchor: "beginning of the conversation", order: "BEFORE". Participants: ["user", "agent"].

2. Only help one user per conversation, deny requests for other users: "You can only help one user per conversation (but you can handle multiple requests from the same user), and must deny any requests for tasks related to any other user."

Modality: REQUIRE to help only one user; FORBID to help other users. Could split into two rules.

Rule 2a: REQUIRE: help only one user per conversation. Target: help user. Condition: per conversation. Exception: null.
